sentences.text: This petition filed by the petitioner under Section 18(3)(b) of the L.A. Act with a prayer to direct the respondent to make a reference under Section 18 of L.A. Act to the Court.

.2. The case made out by the petitioner in the petition in nutshell is that the petitioner is an owner of the land bearing Sy. No. 15/2 measuring 12 guntas of land out of 1 acre 30 guntas of Amani Byrati Khane village and the said property acquired by the petitioner under a registered Will.

It is also stated that the petitioner filed claim statement as on 06.03.2000 claiming compensation @ Rs.
Balachandra V vs Special L A O on 5 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/193158125/
1 25,00,000/- per acre.
It is also stated that the petitioner has no knowledge of the award passed by the LAO and no notice has been served on him.
Further he stated that he came to know about the award only on 06.04.2002 when he received the compensation of Rs.2,22,207/- for his 12 guntas of land.

Accordingly, prayed to direct the respondent to L.A.C. No.32/2003 make a reference of his claim petition dated 06.03.2000.
.3.
The respondent appeared through learned DGP and filed objection statement stating that the said application is not filed within the prescribed period and hence, liable to be dismissed in limine.
Hence, prayed for dismissal of the petition.
.4. To prove his case, the petitioner V. Balachandra is examined as PW.1.
Document got marked at Ex.P.1 to Ex.
P.5 . The respondent has not led any evidence in support of their defence.
.5. On the basis of above, the point for consideration is that.
"Whether the petitioner has made out sufficient grounds to direct the respondent to make a reference under Section 18 of L.A. Act to the Court as prayed in the petition?"

.6. Heard the arguments, perused the materials on record, on that basis, my finding on the above point is in the negative, for the following:
REASONS .7.

The petitioner filed the present petition before the Court as on 31.01.2003 under Section 18(3)(b) of the L.A. Act with a specific prayer to direct the respondent/ SLAO to refer the claim petition submitted by the petitioner as on 06.03.2000 to the Court to determine proper market value on the acquired property claiming that worth of property acquired by the respondent is @ Rs. 25,00,000/- per acre.
Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for compensation.

.8. Before proceeding further in this case, it is just and relevant to note the relevant provision under Section 18 of the L.A. Act and this Court has to follow the said provision of law to entertain the present petition.

In view of the aforesaid fact, it is just and necessary to see Section 18 of the L.A. Act, 1894 that reads as follows:
L.A.C. No.32/2003 "18.

Reference to Court(1)Any person interested who has not accepted the award may, by written application to the Collector, require that the matter be referred by the Collector for the determination of the Court, whether his objection be to the measurement of the land, the amount of the compensation, the persons to whom it is payable, or the apportionment of the compensation among the persons interested.

(2)The application shall state the grounds on which objection to the award is taken:Provided that every such application shall be made,

2 (a)if the person making it was present or represented before the Collector at the time when he made his award, within six weeks from the date of the Collectors award;
(b)in other cases, within six weeks of the receipt of the notice from the Collector under section 12,
sub-section (2), or within six months from the date of the Collectors award, whichever period shall first expire.
(3)(a) The Deputy Commissioner shall, within ninety days from the date of receipt of an application under sub- section (1), make a reference to the Court:

sentences.text: (b) If the Deputy Commissioner does not make a reference to the Court within a period of ninety days from the date of receipt of the application, the applicant may apply to the Court to direct the L.A.C. No.32/2003 Deputy Commissioner to make the reference, and the Court may direct the Deputy Commissioner to make the reference within such time as the Court may fix"
The aforesaid Section 18 of the L.A. Act speaks about the reference to the Court and procedure thereon.

Therefore, to entertain the application under Section 18 of L.A.
Act, the Court has to adopt the procedure contemplated under Section 18 (1) to 18 (3)
of the L.A. Act.

As per Section 18 of the L.A. Act, any person interested who has not accepted the award passed by the land acquisition officer may by written application to the collector, require that the matter be referred by the collector for determination of the Court regarding measurement of the land as well as amount of compensation.

.9. Any reference under Sub Section 1 to Section 18 of L.A. Act is to be in accordance with Section 18(2) of L.A. Act which prescribes certain guidelines or procedure to make a reference or the guidelines to file application L.A.C. No.32/2003 seeking reference of the application for higher compensation.

.10. As per Section 18(2)(a), if the person making the application to the Court was present when the notice has been passed by the LAO or the District Collector, then the application has to be submitted to the District Collector to make a reference within 6 weeks from the date of Collector's award.

.11. Similarly Section 18(2)(b) states that if a person was not present when the award has been passed, then, he has to file an application for reference to the Court to determine the higher compensation within 6 weeks from the date of receipt of notice from the Collector/Land Acquisition Officer under Section 12(2) of the L.A. Act.
.12.
Therefore, any application for reference for enhancement of compensation to be filed after passing of the award or after receipt of the award notice.

If Section 18 of L.A. Act has been taken into consideration, then no application can be filed for making a reference to the L.A.C. No.32/2003 Court before passing of award or before receipt of the award notice.

for the enhancement of compensation before the passing of award or the receipt of notice under Section 12 (2) of the Land Acquisition Act is unknown to the procedure contemplated under the provisions of The Land Acquisition Act.
.13.

In view of the aforesaid clear cut procedure prescribed under law for the making of reference of the application to the court, the petitioner must prove that on which date, the award has been passed or on which date the award notice has been issued.
The petitioner in the entire petition nowhere stated about on which date the award has been passed or on which date the award notice has been issued.

Of course, the petitioner pleaded ignorance about date of passing of the award as well as receipt of award notice but the respondent specifically admitted that the petitioner has the knowledge of passing of the award when he received the compensation amount vide cheque dated 06.04.2002.
Even if it is accepted, then, it has to be accepted that the petitioner has the knowledge of passing of the award as on 06.04.2002.
As such, any application to the District Collector to make a reference under Section 12(2)(b) to be filed within 6 weeks from the date of said date.
Admittedly no application filed by the petitioner to the LAO after receipt of the amount or the alleged knowledge of the passing of award.
.14. At this juncture, it is also relevant to note aforesaid the Karnataka Amendment to Section 18 of L.A. Act by inserting Sub Section 3 to the Section 18.

The plain reading of Section 18(3) makes it clear that the application submitted under Section 18(2)(a)
or (b) of the L.A. Act to the District Collector after knowing about passing of the award or after receipt of the award notice; if the District Collector fails to make a reference within a period of 90 days from the date of receipt of such application, the petitioner can approach the Court by filing an application seeking direction to the SLAO to make the reference by forwarding application submitted L.A.C. No.32/2003 to the Land Acquisition Officer to the court for enhancement of compensation or determine the market value of the acquired property.

Therefore, the procedure prescribed under the Land Acquisition Act makes it clear that the land looser after knowing of the passing of the award or after receipt of the award notice, such land looser shall file an application to refer such application to the competent court for enhancement or to determine the market value.
If there is no such application, then the Court cannot direct the SLAO to make any reference.
.15. In this case, the petitioner got marked the documents.
Ex.P.1 is an application along with endorsement.

The said endorsement is dated 15.11.2002, wherein, the LAO stated that the award notice has been served on one C. Balachandra (petitioner)
as on 05.02.2001 and after receipt of the notice within 90 days no application has been filed before the LAO to make a reference, hence, question of referring the application to the Court to determine the market value does not arise.

Infact according to the said L.A.C. No.32/2003 endorsement, the petitioner has filed an Balachandra V vs Special L A O on 5 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/193158125/
4 application before the LAO as on 07.02.2002 for making the reference.

sentences.text: The said endorsement by the SLAO dated 15.11.2002 is not disputed by the petitioner.
If the said contention in the endorsement is accepted, this petitioner has filed an application before the LAO as on 07.02.2002.
The said fact has been suppressed by the petitioner before the Court.
The petitioner has not at all whispered anything about the said application and copy of the said application is also not produced.
Infact the said document falsifies the claim of petitioner that he came to know about passing of the award when he received the cheque dated 06.04.2002.
Because the said application is two months prior to the receipt of the money.

Therefore, in the case on hand, the petitioner prima facie fails to make out a case to show that after passing of the award or after receipt of award notice,
the petitioner has not filed any application before the LAO.

It is relevant to note that the petitioner is at all seeking direction to the SLAO to make a reference of application L.A.C. No.32/2003 submitted to the LAO subsequent to passing of the award or receipt of the award notice.

The prayer of the petitioner is to refer the application submitted by him to the LAO as on 06.03.2000, which is prior to passing of the award and such application certainly cannot be entertained under Section 18 of the L.A. Act.

Therefore, this Court is of the humble opinion that the petitioner fails to make out a case to show that after passing of the award or service of notice, he has filed any application to the LAO to make a reference.
When there is no such application before the LAO to make a reference, question of direct the LAO to make a reference to the Court does not arise.
Apart from that, there is no material on record to show that subsequent application is also filed within the limitation period.

Therefore, this Court is of the humble opinion that the petitioner fails to make out sufficient grounds to issue direction to the Deputy Commissioner / LAO to make a reference to the Court to decide the market value of the acquired property.
Hence, I answer the above point in the negative, for the following:
ORDER The petition filed by the petitioner u/s.18(3)(b) of L.A. Act, 1894 is hereby dismissed.
